_note: Town urine and nightsoil, and the market garden that spreads nightsoil (Complaints/544). No recipe lets a household output a good, so people's excreta enter the economy through collection recipes: the kilograms a person voids in a year are stated on each (excreted_kg_per_person_year, a physical fact for a test to read), the labour is gathering and carrying. Urine is bought by fullers and tanners (40_organics.json), nightsoil by market gardens below.

urine_kg.extracted_from: town households (urine voided into jars and privies)
urine_kg.basis: per tonne of urine collected from town households and carried to the works
urine_kg.yield_basis: COLLECTED. An adult voids on the order of one and a half litres of urine a day, about 550 kg a year (Rose et al., The Characterization of Feces and Urine, Critical Reviews in Environmental Science and Technology 45 (2015), PMC4500995, opened: "A median volume of 1.4 L/cap/day urine is excreted with mean values ranging from 0.6 to 2.6 L/cap/day"; conf C), of which urine is about a thousand and ten grams a litre. Gathering is emptying street jars and household pots into a barrel and carrying it a short way: twelve labourer hours a tonne (author's estimate, conf D). The supply a town can give is its people times the excreted figure times the share collected; the share is not modelled, so the labour is the only limit (a limit that needs households to output goods; see the resolution in Complaints/closed/544). Sole output, so the cost is the collection labour.

nightsoil_kg.basis: per tonne of nightsoil (privy contents, faeces and urine together) collected and carried out of town
nightsoil_kg.yield_basis: COLLECTED. Faeces are on the order of 100 to 150 g wet a day, about 50 kg a person-year, and the urine that goes down the same privy another 550 kg, so about 600 kg of mixed nightsoil (Rose et al. 2015, PMC4500995, opened: "the median fecal wet mass production was 128 g/cap/day"; conf C). Emptying a pit, loading buckets and carrying them to a cart is slow, foul work: twenty labourer hours a tonne (author's estimate, conf D; Pass 11: F. H. King, Farmers of Forty Centuries, ch. 9, https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Farmers_of_forty_centuries/Chapter_09, opened, takes 'the average amount of excreta per day for the adult at 40 ounces', about 910 lb or 414 kg a year, against the 600 kg a year here, which also counts the household's urine; the 20 collection hours a tonne have no source found). The supply a town can give is its people times the excreted figure times the share collected; the share is not modelled, so the labour is the only limit. Sole output, so the cost is the collection labour.

vegetable_kg.basis: per hectare of market garden cropped for one year, as kg of fresh vegetables (cabbage, onion, beet, legumes in pod) sold to the town
vegetable_kg.yield_basis: GROWN. A hand-worked garden beside a town, cropped more than once a year on ground manured heavily with nightsoil: fifteen tonnes fresh a hectare is the low end of intensive garden yields (no source found; Columella's De re rustica book 10 and F. H. King, Farmers of Forty Centuries, 1911, were not opened; conf D). Nightsoil is applied at about twenty tonnes a hectare a year in the Chinese practice King describes (King, ch. 9, https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Farmers_of_forty_centuries/Chapter_09, opened, gives Japan's 1908 application as 1.75 tons per acre averaged over all cultivated land, about 4.4 tonnes a hectare, so a heavily dunged garden at 20 is plausible but not bounded; no source found for a garden rate; conf D). Labour: digging, bedding, watering, weeding and picking by hand, about eighteen hundred hours a hectare (author's estimate; Pass 11: John Hendrickson, market-farming mailing list post summarising six Wisconsin market gardens under 3 acres, https://lists.ibiblio.org/sympa/arc/market-farming/2005-06/msg00158.html, opened: 'just under 2000 total labor hours per acre', about 4900 hours a hectare for modern small gardens, 2.7 times this figure, so 1800 is at the low end; conf D). LAND: one hectare-year charged at hectare_land's rent like wheat_kg. The soil has no nutrient stock in the model (Complaints/543), so the nightsoil is a cost of the garden's yield, not a restoration of a pool. Food value is a tenth of wheat grain a kilogram (data/world/needs.json).
